messages:
aurora-cse: Hey team, Aurora ops here — customers started seeing intermittent 429s and latency spikes from their dedicated pool (aurora-prod-dedicated-v2) around 2026-03-15 15:29 UTC. They report tail latency 2s->5s then 429 'pool_overload'. Any quick triage?

maya: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste a sample request id + short repro? Also which model/sequence length are they serving?

aurora-cse: sample req id req_8a1b. Model: redwood/gptx-13b, avg seq ~512 tokens. Repro: run a bursty load test (simulated customers) — 1s ramp to ~800 rps for ~20s. 429 message payload: {"error":"rate_limited","reason":"burst_limit_exceeded","pool":"aurora-prod-dedicated-v2"}.

sam: looking at infra metrics now — autoscaler didn't start adding replicas until ~40s after the QPS spike. Baseline ~110 rps, spike to ~820 rps at 15:29:34. Pool shows 12 replicas. I also see GPU queue depth climb and one node with sustained kernel contention.

ingrid: can you paste the autoscaler policy? cooldowns, target metrics? noisy neighbor signs (OOMs, MIG shifts, GPU memory pressure)?

aurora-cse: here is the autoscaler snippet they gave us:

```
autoscaler:
  minReplicas: 12
  maxReplicas: 24
  metric: requests_per_second
  target: 600
  scaleUpCooldown: 60
  scaleDownCooldown: 300
```

maya: hm — target:600 RPS for the whole pool looks odd relative to minReplicas. If target is per-pool and not per-replica, scale decisions can lag for short but large bursts. Also scaleUpCooldown 60s is long for bursty traffic.

sam: adding to that, the node-level metrics show GPU-0 on node-3 with much higher avg GPU util and a longer kernel queue. Looks like a single replica was handling heavier work (noisy neighbor). I captured a short snippet from the node: 

```
node-3 GPU-0: avg_util 92% queue_depth 53 tail_latency 1.8s
node-3 GPU-1: avg_util 48% queue_depth 12 tail_latency 0.6s
```

ingrid: immediate mitigations we can do:
- add burst_capacity=true for this pool so short spikes don't 429 while scaler reacts
- reduce scaleUpCooldown from 60s -> 15s to allow faster ramp-up
- add a soft routing fallback to hosted API for non-sensitive tenant traffic
- evict the noisy replica or migrate pod off node-3 while we debug kernel-level hotspot

maya: sizing guidance (rough calc): baseline sustained 110 rps, peak observed 820 rps. If we target 55% utilization for the chosen model/profile and assume ~90 rps per GPU at seq512, then needed GPUs for peak = ceil(820 / (90 * 0.55)) ~ 17. MinReplicas 12 is underprovisioned for peak bursts unless burst_capacity is enabled. Recommend minReplicas=14, maxReplicas=30, targetPerPool=800 (or switch to per-replica target), and faster scale-up.

jorge: pinging customer ops: we're going to enable burst capacity and temporarily lower scaleUpCooldown. Also will enable client-side exponential backoff on their SDK to reduce retry storms. I've asked them to hold non-critical background jobs for the next 2 hours.

aurora-cse: noted — we enabled client backoff and queued background jobs. We still see a few 429s during the next spike window but far fewer. Thanks.

maya: action items: 
- maya -> open infra escalation to enable burst_capacity for aurora-prod-dedicated-v2 and evict noisy pod (ETA 1h)
- ingrid -> propose updated autoscaler YAML and run a dry-run simulation against historical traces (ETA 2h)
- jorge -> coordinate temporary hosted fallback routing and customer comms (ETA 30m)

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-AURORA created by maya.

jorge: customer confirmed fewer 429s after client backoff + our temporary changes. We'll monitor through peak windows tonight. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll follow up with postmortem and capacity plan (incl. model profile, seq distribution, expected QPS tiers). Keeping this thread open until autoscaler changes land.

aurora-cse: thanks all, appreciate the quick help — will keep posting logs here if anything new pops up.
